properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. O-21 of the hxm_program hub's 2026-09-28 report (art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28). Host and controller names are redacted because this export is public.

THE REPORTER'S WORDS: "Plant-inventory adoption and drift. /adopt for the physical side, from sources the facility already maintains:
- control-system screen files (which controller and axis carry which motor, and which IOC and host serve it);
- `manage-iocs status` output (which IOCs run where).
Then flag drift between them. Today, by hand: the [controller] info screen says [its] IOC is on [host A], and the live host list says [host B]. `hosts.html` does this job manually, and the 'reverse drift' note is how it gets out of step."

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS NEARBY: reflow2 has an as-fielded reconcile, cap:reconcile-deployed (reconcile_deployment, BL-9). It compares DECLARED deployments (Release DEPLOYED_TO Environment) with OBSERVED running releases, and records DriftEvents that resolve themselves when a later observation agrees. By construction it leaves Components out ("Components never participate"), because the original reflow manufactured false drift for every library. The report's second example is exactly that shape: which IOC runs on which host, declared against observed.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) A PHYSICAL ADOPT PASS: read screen files and IOC-manager status into Components (controllers, axes, IOCs, hosts) with allocations, marked inferred, then reconcile them against each fresh observation. Large, because the readers are specific to one facility's file formats.
(b) DRIFT WITHOUT ADOPTION: the design holds only the declared side (as Releases and Environments do today), and a reconcile compares it with the observed side each time. Medium, if reconcile_deployment's observed side is widened from Releases to named assets, which reverses a limit it chose on purpose.
(c) THE FACILITY'S OWN INVENTORY STAYS THE SOURCE: the hub's host list (or the facility's asset database) is registered as an Artifact, and a project-side script does the comparison. Small for reflow2.
(d) ONLY ON DEMAND: incidents pull assets into existence one at a time (O-17, dec:idea-an-incident-is-a-low-ceremony-record-hung-on-a-named-asset), with no bulk adoption. Depends on O-17.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
· Parsers for one facility's screen files and service manager are not a design tool's job. reflow2's schema is domain-neutral, and every site has different sources, so this belongs in an adapter the project owns.
· Fewer things well (dec:idea-reflow2-does-fewer-things-and-does-them-really-well): a plant inventory with drift detection is a configuration-management database, a mature product category. This is the strongest pull away from the core identity among this report's ideas.
· The drift the reporter names is between two EXTERNAL sources, not between the design and reality. reflow2's reconciles compare the design with the world. Comparing two outside records with each other makes reflow2 a data-quality checker for someone else's systems.
· FOR it: the reporter describes /adopt pointed at a set of existing repos as how the hub started, and the physical plant is the half /adopt cannot see. The as-fielded reconcile shows the declared-against-observed shape is already part of reflow2's design. And a hand-kept host list drifting silently is the coherence failure reflow2 exists to prevent.

2026-09-28, LATER THE SAME DAY: the question this idea depends on is settled. Anthony: reflow2 serves a design for its whole life, concept → operations, and the loop runs as long as the system lives (dec:idea-reflow2-serves-a-design-in-operations-where-incidents-feed-the-design, accepted). The dependency is met. What stays open here is HOW the physical plant is brought under the design, and the counter-arguments above weigh the how, never whether operations belongs in reflow2. Where this text or its DEPENDS_ON evidence speaks of the umbrella's options, those options are withdrawn: the question was never open (fact:root-cause-the-lifecycle-scope-lives-in-the-vision-and-the-graph-holds-one-line-so-a-brainstorm-reopened-it-2026-09-28).
properties.name: OPEN — should /adopt take in the PHYSICAL side of an operating system from the sources a facility already keeps (control-system screen files, the IOC manager's status output), and flag drift between those sources?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill (fetched fresh) during the triage of art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28. Searched first (adopt physical plant inventory, hardware asset drift, reconcile as-fielded): the nearest are the as-fielded reconcile capability, which has the declared-against-observed shape but excludes components on purpose, the physical-domains idea from the xrt-demo and bhome reports (ordered parts, dimensioned quantities, a physical medium), which is about designing physical systems rather than inventorying them, and the umbrella operations question.
